### workspace ask --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace ask [WS] "<question>" --default "<default taken>" [options]
       workspace ask list [WS] [--all] [--json]
       workspace ask answer [WS] <id> "<answer>" [--deliver] [--json]
       workspace ask deliver [WS] <id> [--pane P] [--json]
       workspace ask withdraw [WS] <id> [--json]

Records a question an unattended agent hit, with the default it took,
so the agent can keep going instead of blocking on a person. Never
reads stdin; returns once the question is recorded and any notify
command has finished (it is stopped after 10 seconds).

Subcommands:
  list                    Show open questions for this workspace (--all: also answered
                          and withdrawn ones, with their status)
  answer <id> <answer>    Resolve an open question (alias: resolve); with --deliver,
                          also type the answer and Enter into the pane that asked
  deliver <id>            Type an answered question's answer and Enter into its pane again
                          (the retry when `answer --deliver` saved the answer but could not type it;
                          check the pane first, this types the answer again);
                          --pane P types into another pane of the workspace instead
  withdraw <id>           Close an open question nobody needs answered any more; it
                          leaves `ask list` and the inbox, and can't be answered

A first word of list, answer, resolve, deliver, withdraw or help is a subcommand only
without --default; `workspace ask list --default x` records "list".

Options (every subcommand):
  --name WS         Act on workspace WS instead of the one detected from the
                    current directory (the same as the WS argument); outside any
                    workspace and with neither, the command fails with not_in_workspace

Options (deliver):
  --pane P          Type into pane P (a pane id or window.pane of the workspace's
                    own tmux session) instead of the pane that asked

Options (answer):
  --deliver         Type the answer, then Enter, into the pane that asked, which must
                    belong to the workspace's tmux session. The pane is checked before the
                    question is answered; if typing then fails, the question stays
                    answered and the error says so. Needs a question asked from tmux.
  --                Ends options, so an answer starting with "-" works

Options (recording a question):
  --default TEXT    The default the agent took (required)
  --context TEXT    Free-text pointer to the code in question, e.g. "file.rb:42"
  --json             Emit the documented JSON schema instead of a message

When the project has `alerts.notify` configured (see
`workspace config set alerts.notify <command>`), it runs with
WORKSPACE_ALERT=question and the question/default in
WORKSPACE_ALERT_* env vars. Without it, the question is just recorded.

Run `workspace ask VERB --help` for the page of one subcommand.

Examples:
  workspace ask "Use pg or sqlite for the cache?" --default "sqlite"    # record a question and keep going with the default
  workspace ask "Use pg or sqlite?" --default "sqlite" --context "lib/cache.rb:12"    # point at the code in question
  workspace ask list    # open questions of this workspace
  workspace ask list myapp --all    # another workspace's, answered and withdrawn ones too
  workspace ask answer a1b2c3 "Use postgres instead"    # answer an open question
  workspace ask answer --deliver a1b2c3 "yes"    # also type the answer into the pane that asked
  workspace ask deliver a1b2c3    # type the saved answer again after a failed delivery
  workspace ask withdraw a1b2c3    # the asker no longer needs an answer
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace ask list --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace ask list [WS] [--all] [--json]

Show the open questions of a workspace.

WS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.
Without --all only open questions are shown; a workspace with none prints a line saying so.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --all                        Also list answered and withdrawn questions, with their status
    --json                       Print the documented JSON document instead of a message
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace ask list    # open questions of the workspace of the current directory
  workspace ask list myapp    # another workspace's open questions
  workspace ask list --all    # answered and withdrawn questions too, with a STATUS column
  workspace ask list --json    # one JSON document, for a script
--- stderr
--- end

--- stdout

### workspace ask answer --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace ask answer [WS] ID "ANSWER" [--deliver] [--json]

Answer an open question (alias: resolve).

WS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.
The answer is saved on the question, which then leaves the open list; a question already answered
or withdrawn is refused (exit 1). End options with -- to give an answer that starts with a dash.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --deliver                    Also type the answer and Enter into the pane that asked (it must be a pane of this workspace's tmux session; the question must have been asked from tmux)
    --json                       Print the documented JSON document instead of a message
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace ask answer a1b2c3 "Use postgres instead"    # answer a question of this workspace
  workspace ask answer myapp a1b2c3 "Use postgres instead"    # answer a question of another workspace
  workspace ask answer --deliver a1b2c3 "yes"    # also type the answer into the pane that asked
  workspace ask answer a1b2c3 -- "-1"    # an answer that starts with a dash
  workspace ask answer a1b2c3 "yes" --json    # print the answered question as JSON
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace ask answer --help --json

--- stdout

End options with -- to give an answer that starts with a dash.","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--deliver","description":"Also type the answer and Enter into the pane that asked (it must be a pane of this workspace's tmux session; the question must have been asked from tmux)"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print the documented JSON document instead of a message"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace ask answer a1b2c3 \"Use postgres instead\"","scenario":"answer a question of this workspace"},{"command":"workspace ask answer myapp a1b2c3 \"Use postgres instead\"","scenario":"answer a question of another workspace"},{"command":"workspace ask answer --deliver a1b2c3 \"yes\"","scenario":"also type the answer into the pane that asked"},{"command":"workspace ask answer a1b2c3 -- \"-1\"","scenario":"an answer that starts with a dash"},{"command":"workspace ask answer a1b2c3 \"yes\" --json","scenario":"print the answered question as JSON"}]}
--- stderr

### workspace ask deliver --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace ask deliver [WS] ID [--pane PANE] [--json]

Type an answered question's answer, then Enter, into its pane again.

WS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.
The retry for when `ask answer --deliver` saved the answer but could not type it. Nothing is saved;
the pane is typed into for real, so check it first: the answer goes in again even if the first try landed.
A question that is still open or withdrawn has no answer to deliver (exit 1).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --pane PANE                  Type into this pane (an id such as %19, or window.pane) of the workspace's own session instead of the pane that asked
    --json                       Print the documented JSON document instead of a message
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace ask deliver a1b2c3    # retype the answer into the pane that asked
  workspace ask deliver myapp a1b2c3    # the same for another workspace's question
  workspace ask deliver a1b2c3 --pane %19    # type it into another pane of the workspace's session
  workspace ask deliver a1b2c3 --json    # print the question and the pane typed into as JSON
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace ask deliver --help --json
--- exit 0
--- stdout
{"usage":["workspace ask deliver [WS] ID [--pane PANE] [--json]"],"description":"Type an answered question's answer, then Enter, into its pane again.\n\nWS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.\nThe retry for when `ask answer --deliver` saved the answer but could not type it. Nothing is saved;\nthe pane is typed into for real, so check it first: the answer goes in again even if the first try landed.\nA question that is still open or withdrawn has no answer to deliver (exit 1).","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--pane PANE","description":"Type into this pane (an id such as %19, or window.pane) of the workspace's own session instead of the pane that asked"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print the documented JSON document instead of a message"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace ask deliver a1b2c3","scenario":"retype the answer into the pane that asked"},{"command":"workspace ask deliver myapp a1b2c3","scenario":"the same for another workspace's question"},{"command":"workspace ask deliver a1b2c3 --pane %19","scenario":"type it into another pane of the workspace's session"},{"command":"workspace ask deliver a1b2c3 --json","scenario":"print the question and the pane typed into as JSON"}]}
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace ask withdraw --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace ask withdraw [WS] ID [--json]

Close an open question nobody needs answered any more.

WS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.
The question is marked withdrawn: it leaves `ask list` and the inbox and can't be answered. Only an
open question can be withdrawn (exit 1 otherwise).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print the documented JSON document instead of a message
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace ask withdraw a1b2c3    # the asker no longer needs an answer
  workspace ask withdraw myapp a1b2c3    # withdraw a question of another workspace
  workspace ask withdraw a1b2c3 --json    # print the withdrawn question as JSON
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace ask withdraw --help --json
--- exit 0
--- stdout
{"usage":["workspace ask withdraw [WS] ID [--json]"],"description":"Close an open question nobody needs answered any more.\n\nWS is a workspace name; without it (or --name) the workspace of the current directory is used.\nThe question is marked withdrawn: it leaves `ask list` and the inbox and can't be answered. Only an\nopen question can be withdrawn (exit 1 otherwise).","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print the documented JSON document instead of a message"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace ask withdraw a1b2c3","scenario":"the asker no longer needs an answer"},{"command":"workspace ask withdraw myapp a1b2c3","scenario":"withdraw a question of another workspace"},{"command":"workspace ask withdraw a1b2c3 --json","scenario":"print the withdrawn question as JSON"}]}
--- stderr
--- end
